metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded from 64 channels in DC mode (reference: right mastoid) with electrode locations digitized for source analysis. Bifocal MRI-navigated TMS targeted the first dorsal interossei representation in bilateral primary motor cortex. Paired associative stimulation consisted of left M1 stimulation at t=0 ms followed by right M1 stimulation at asynchronies of 4, 9, or 14 ms across three sessions. Single-pulse TMS at 100% or 110% resting motor threshold was delivered before, 10 minutes after, and 60 minutes after ccPAS. Resting-state EEG (eyes open, fixation) was collected at baseline, pre-ccPAS, and post-ccPAS timepoints. MRI protocols included T1-weighted structural imaging, resting-state fMRI, and HARDI diffusion imaging (SMS 271 directions) in subsets of participants.

citation_details.title: Metastability indexes global network effects post brain stimulation
citation_details.author: Rishabh Bapat, Anagh Pathak, Arpan Banerjee
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Several studies have shown that coordination among neural ensembles is a key to understand human cognition. A well charted path is to identify coordination states associated with cognitive functions from spectral changes in the oscillations of EEG or MEG. A growing number of studies suggest that the tendency to switch between coordination states, sculpts the dynamic repertoire of the brain and can be indexed by a measure known as metastability. In this article, we characterize perturbations in the metastability of global brain network dynamics following Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation that could quantify the duration for which information processing is altered, thus, allowing researchers to understand the network effects of brain stimulation, standardise stimulation protocols and design experimental tasks. We demonstrate the effect empirically using publicly available datasets and use a digital twin (a whole brain connectome model) to understand the dynamic principles that generate such observations. We observed a significant reduction in metastability, concurrent with an increase in coherence following single-pulse TMS reflecting the existence of a window where neural coordination is altered. The reduction in complexity was validated by an additional measure based on the Lempel-Ziv complexity of microstate labelled EEG data. Interestingly, higher frequencies in the EEG signal showed faster recovery in metastability than lower frequencies. The digital twin shed light on how the phase resetting introduced by the single-pulse TMS in local cortical networks can propagate globally across the whole brain and give rise to changes in metastability and coherence.

citation_details.title: GFEX-EEG — Paper Analysis Code Bundle
citation_details.author: Michael McMahon, Michael Schukat, Enda Barrett
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Analysis and figure-generation scripts reproducing the results, tables, and figures of the manuscript 'GFEX-EEG: Geodesic recovery of anatomical fiducials for MRI-free EEG source imaging' (McMahon, Schukat, Barrett). Includes per-cohort HTJ scoreboards, 3-point Procrustes and ICP baselines, ICP and PCAwarp A/B preprocessor evaluations, cohort-specific MLP training, the annotation-floor TOST equivalence analysis, the source-localization simulation, and figure scripts. Distinct from the GFEX-EEG toolbox (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20580899). Reproduction requires the public cohorts (ds000221, ds000117/ds002718, ds004024, ds005795) and per-subject HTJ tags (available from the corresponding author on request).

citation_details.title: GFEX-EEG Validation Database: Brainstorm-tagged head models with manual helix-tragus-junction fiducials
citation_details.author: Michael McMahon, Michael Schukat, Enda Barrett
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Processed Brainstorm head-model database used to validate the GFEX-EEG toolbox (Geodesic Fiducial Extrapolation for MRI-free EEG source imaging). For four per-subject EEG–MRI cohorts it provides the imported, defaced structural MRIs, the derived Brainstorm anatomical surfaces, and the manually-tagged helix-tragus-junction (HTJ) ground-truth fiducials (Brainstorm SCS fiducial structures, with SCS.LPA/RPA holding the left/right HTJ) that underlie every accuracy number reported in the GFEX-EEG manuscript. Each cohort is provided as a self-contained, Brainstorm-loadable ZIP archive (a complete Brainstorm protocol with anat/ and data/ folders): • LEMON — MPI-Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body (OpenNeuro ds000221 / NITRC Fcon_1000; Polhemus digitizer) • Wakeman-Henson — subject-correct "rescued" EEG–MRI pairing (OpenNeuro ds000117 + ds002718; Neuromag/Elekta) • Shirley Ryan AbilityLab — TMS-EEG-MRI-fMRI-DWI (OpenNeuro ds004024; BrainProducts CapTrak) • MULTI-CLARID — Leibniz Institute, Magdeburg (OpenNeuro ds005795) Ground-truth convention: the helix-tragus junction was tagged manually in Brainstorm's MRI viewer for every MRI-bearing subject; in each subject's anat/.../subjectimage_*.mat the fields SCS.LPA and SCS.RPA hold the left/right HTJ (not the conventional pre-auricular point), and SCS.NAS is the standard nasion. All reported GFEX-EEG errors are therefore true HTJ accuracy. Privacy: all structural MRIs are defaced. They are imported unmodified in facial content from source datasets that distribute them already defaced (LEMON; Wakeman-Henson; OpenNeuro-mandated defacing for ds004024; pydeface for ds005795), confirmed by source documentation and by direct visual inspection across all four cohorts. The brain is preserved; the identifiable facial surface is removed. Licensing: the GFEX-EEG curation layer in this record — the manual HTJ tagging, the Brainstorm head-model organization, and the selection/compilation — is released under CC BY 4.0. The underlying source neuroimaging data remain under their original public-domain dedications (LEMON: PDDL; Wakeman-Henson, Shirley Ryan, MULTI-CLARID: CC0) and are not relicensed. Please cite both this record and the original source datasets (see the included README.md). Related resources: GFEX-EEG toolbox (https://github.com/michaelmcmahon/GFEX-EEG; Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20580898) and the GFEX-EEG paper-analysis bundle (https://github.com/michaelmcmahon/GFEX-EEG-paper-analysis; Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20800437).
